chunks: From him, from Ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskhan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about giving one egg for two eggs. He said, 'There is no objection.' And about giving one garment for two garments. He said, 'There is no objection.' And about giving one horse for two horses. He said, 'There is no objection.' Then he said, 'Everything that is measured by volume or weight, it is not valid to give two of the same kind for one. But if it is not measured or weighed, there is no objection to giving two for one.'

key_terms.مِثْلَيْنِ بِمِثْلٍ: two of the same kind for one

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in exchange rules between measured and unmeasured goods in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *riba al-fadl* (excess in same-kind exchange) and general barter by categorizing goods based on whether they are typically measured (*mukayyaf*) or weighed (*mawzuna*). It establishes that while exchanging two units of a measured commodity for one unit of the same kind is prohibited to prevent hidden interest, such restriction does not apply to non-measured items like horses or garments, where 'two for one' is permissible. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the functional nature of the commodity rather than a rigid list of specific items.
